claim: Samoan syllables have the template (C)V(V): onsets are optional, while codas and consonant clusters are not allowed.
scope: tautala lelei register; descriptive generalization attributed by Kuo to Mosel & Hovdhaugen 1992

claim: Stress is non-contrastive: it falls on a final long vowel, otherwise on the penultimate vowel; suffixation can shift stress, with the effect dependent on suffix size.
normalized_environment: Stress→Vː#; else penultimate V; suffix-size conditioned
scope: word stress; Kuo cites Zuraw et al. 2014
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Suffixation may shift stress and the shift depends on suffix size.

claim: Vowel-vowel sequences may occur as hiatus or diphthongs; Kuo treats /ai, au, ei, ou/ as diphthongs because they pattern like long vowels in stress.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Mosel & Hovdhaugen 1992 propose a larger diphthong set additionally including /eo, oi, ui/.

claim: Phonemic /ʔ/ is unstable word-initially and is elided except in very careful speech.
scope: initial position; quotation attributed to Mosel & Hovdhaugen 1992
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The glottal stop may be retained in very careful speech.

claim: /k, r, h/ are restricted to loanwords or interjections rather than inherited native vocabulary; /r/ is often realized as [l] even in careful speech.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: /r/ may surface as [l] even in careful speech.

claim: The tautala leaga register has three mergers relative to tautala lelei: /t,k/→/k/, /n,ŋ/→/ŋ/, and /r,l/→/l/.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Two mergers involve phonemes Kuo identifies as loan-associated (/k/ and /r/).

claim: Stem phonotactics show a strong gradient dispreference for labial-labial consonant pairs and for coronal-coronal pairs that also match in sonorancy.
normalized_environment: *C[place=α] ... C[place=α], strengthened when coronal pair matches sonorancy
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The restrictions are gradient, not categorical.

claim: In the fitted OCP model, OCP-LAB, OCP-COR-SON, and OCP-BACK are significant, whereas general OCP-place and the other tested place/sonorancy refinements are not.
normalized_environment: OCP constraints over consonant pairs, controlling baseline consonant frequencies
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Several intuitively related OCP constraints receive no independent support in the fitted model.

claim: Sequences /ŋ...m/ and /ŋ...v/ are unattested in the corpus, but Kuo explicitly treats these as potentially accidental gaps rather than established phonotactic bans.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Kuo notes the gaps may be accidental and may partly reflect a Polynesian positional preference for labials initially and dorsals non-initially.

claim: A Proto-Polynesian corpus shows the same three significant place-cooccurrence effects as modern Samoan: OCP-LAB, OCP-COR-SON, and OCP-BACK.
normalized_environment: OCP place constraints over consonant pairs in PPn stems
scope: POLLEX-derived corpus after removing reduplication, compounds and common affixes
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Consonants are grouped by their Samoan reflex for comparability; general OCP-place and other refinements are non-significant.

time_scope: historical comparison Proto-Oceanic to modern Samoan
claim: Coronal-sonorant sequences such as historical [ilo-na] are disproportionately lost under reanalysis: [l...n] stems occur in Proto-Oceanic (n=11 for the cited type) but are unattested in modern Samoan suffixed forms.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Proto-Oceanic itself shows an [l...n] vs [n...l] asymmetry; Kuo argues the Samoan reanalysis reflects the more general coronal-sonorant restriction rather than memorization of that directional gap.

claim: Phonotactic markedness increases as consonant pairs become spectrally more similar; the relationship is strongest within a shared place of articulation, and coronal-coronal pairs show R²=0.74.
normalized_environment: phonotactic Harmony ∝ inverse spectral distance, especially within-place pairs
scope: acoustic spectral-distance analysis linked to phonotactic Harmony scores
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The labial subset shows weaker correlation because nearly all labial-labial sequences have uniformly high Harmony scores.
